skill.name: healthcare-job-search

content.user_title: Find US Healthcare Jobs and Compare Posted Pay
content.value_statement: Healthcare job searches often require checking many employer sites and separating posted pay from broader salary estimates. This skill uses CareJobs.Now to find openings, compare posted hourly pay, and provide application links.
actual_capabilities: Search healthcare openings by keywords, job type, state, shift, and pay filters through the documented MCP tools.
Present matching jobs with employer, location, posted pay, and an application link.
Retrieve median and typical employer-posted hourly pay by job type.
Retrieve job and employer counts by state or job type within a state.
Query covered employers, individual employer jobs, and healthcare market totals.
Read public pay and role summaries through JSON endpoints when an MCP client is unavailable.
limitations: Coverage is limited to US employers included in CareJobs.Now, not every healthcare opening.
Posted pay is not actual earnings and excludes shift differentials and bonuses.
Job search requires the hosted MCP tools; public JSON endpoints provide pay and role summaries rather than equivalent search.
The skill provides instructions, not a bundled search engine; results depend on external service availability and data freshness.

use_cases.title: Find nursing openings by shift
use_cases.description: Search a city for nursing roles with a preferred shift and compare available posted pay and application links.
use_cases.target_user: Registered nurses seeking a new position

use_cases.title: Compare allied health pay
use_cases.description: Review employer-posted hourly pay for related healthcare roles while keeping posted rates separate from total compensation.
use_cases.target_user: Allied health professionals considering a career change

use_cases.title: Research regional hiring
use_cases.description: Compare job and employer counts across states and identify covered employers with relevant openings.

prompt_templates.title: Find local openings
prompt_templates.prompt: Find CNA jobs near Austin, Texas. Include employer, location, posted hourly pay, and an application link for each match.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: search one role and location.

prompt_templates.title: Filter by shift and pay
prompt_templates.prompt: Find night-shift ICU nursing jobs in Boston with posted pay of at least $40 per hour. Clearly identify any unavailable pay information.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: combine role, location, shift, and pay requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize posted pay
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve respiratory therapist posted hourly pay statistics. Report the median, typical range, sample count, and source, and explain the compensation exclusions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: interpret pay statistics without treating them as actual earnings.

prompt_templates.title: Compare regional opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare nursing job and employer counts in Ohio and Michigan. Identify covered employers and list relevant openings with posted pay and application links. Separate statewide counts from any broader pay statistics.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine state summaries, employer research, and job search.

output_examples.input: What would a healthcare pay summary include?
output: Illustrative format, not live data: Role: respiratory therapist.
Median posted hourly pay: use the returned median; mark unavailable values explicitly.
Typical range: use the returned low and high values, with the available sample count.
These figures describe employer-posted rates on open jobs, not actual earnings, and exclude shift differentials and bonuses.

output_examples.input: How should results appear when no openings match my filters?
output_examples.output: Illustrative response: No matching openings were returned for your role, location, shift, and pay filters. Consider a nearby location or a related role. I cannot provide an application link without a matching listing.

best_practices: Specify the job type, location, preferred shift, and minimum posted pay before searching.
Verify each listing and its compensation details on the employer application page.
Cite CareJobs.Now and distinguish posted hourly rates from actual earnings and total compensation.
anti_patterns: Inventing job listings, application links, or pay figures when the service returns no matching data.
Treating posted hourly pay as guaranteed earnings or assuming missing pay means an unpaid position.
Presenting covered-employer counts as the complete US healthcare labor market.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools. MCP access or HTTP retrieval must be available for live data.

faq.question: Does the service require an API key?
faq.answer: The skill documents a hosted MCP server that requires no API key, plus public JSON endpoints.

faq.question: Does it search jobs outside the United States?
faq.answer: No. The documented scope is US healthcare employers covered by CareJobs.Now.

faq.question: Are the pay figures actual employee earnings?
faq.answer: No. They describe employer-posted hourly rates on open jobs, before shift differentials and bonuses.

faq.question: Can I use it without an MCP client?
faq.answer: Public JSON endpoints provide pay and role summaries without an MCP client. The documented filtered job search uses MCP tools.

faq.question: Does the skill submit job applications?
faq.answer: No application-submission workflow is documented. It returns job links so users can review listings and apply through the relevant employer.
